newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian primary dealers see steady German rates.
newsitem.headline: Belgian primary dealers see steady German rates.

text.p: The Belgian Primary Dealers Association said there was no ground for the Bundesbank to change its interest rate policy now.
"For the time being, the German central bank has no reason to change the course of its monetary policy," it said in its latest newsletter published on Friday.

It added Belgian Treasury bill dealers continued to hope for slightly lower rates, which was encouraging the Treasury to favour shorter maturities in its offerings. "This behaviour is likely to persist at least as long as the market continues to hope for somewhat lower rates."

At the end of January, the share of three-month bills stood at 50.3 percent of the total market, up from 41.1 percent at the end of January 1996. The increase was mainly at the expense of six-month paper. Its share fell to 18.7 percent from 25.8 percent.

But there was little interest in short-term cash bonds since the environment was one of "very low and extremely stable interest rates, in which no one expects the conduct of monetary policy to be significantly changed in the near future," it said.
